chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Wassha' from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no harm with the fish that the Magians catch.'

key_terms.السَّمَكِ: The fish, the subject of the legal ruling regarding its consumption.
key_terms.الْمَجُوسُ: The Magians, referring to Zoroastrians or fire-worshippers in Islamic jurisprudence.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm, a legal phrase indicating permissibility or lack of objection.

ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by Magians halal for Shia Muslims?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify that the general permissibility of fish extends to those caught by the Majus (Zoroastrians), whose status as 'People of the Book' allows their fishing methods to be considered valid. This ruling highlights the Shia principle that the impurity or ritual status of the catcher does not automatically invalidate the fish, provided the species itself is permissible, thereby distinguishing between the purity of the entity and the validity of the act of capture.
